intro: Ordered from easiest to hardest. Start at the top, mark where you are, and note the words you meet: they become the next drill.
tips: Read the Hebrew first. Look at the English only after a paragraph you did not follow.
Look up only what blocks the plot. Guess the rest from the root: a word you do not know is often a binyan you do.
Note five words a session, with the root (נִשְׁאַר, ש־א־ר, to stay). Copy them here and paste them into the chat.
Most real Hebrew has no points. Where a site prints them, read once with them and once covering them up.
Prose from before 1948 spells the old way when it drops the points, and some of its words have moved on. Read it for the story, not as a model for your own Hebrew.
The Bible and the writers who imitated it tell stories with the vav that flips the tense. Recognise it, never produce it: the table below is all you need.

older.title: Biblical Hebrew at a glance
older.note: A וַ with a dagesh on a future-looking verb is the narrative past. The chapter on Biblical Hebrew has the rest.
rows: and it came to pass, there was
and it will be: a past form with a future meaning

groups.title: B1: in this app
groups.note: Written to the course: only grammar you have covered, every hard word glossed, questions at the end.

items.title: הָרַכֶּבֶת הָאַחֲרוֹנָה
items.author: HaMachberet
items.blurb: A night train that will not leave, a father's old story, and a stranger who knew him. One passage, glossed, with questions.

items.title: הַשּׁוּתָּפָה הַחֲדָשָׁה
items.author: HaMachberet
items.blurb: Two candidates for a spare room, a week of hesitating, and one phone call too late. One passage, glossed, with questions.

items.title: הַיְרוּשָּׁה, פְּרָקִים א-ה
items.author: HaMachberet
items.blurb: A lawyer's letter reaches Haifa about a great-aunt Ido had almost forgotten, and a flat in Jerusalem with someone already inside. A serial, one chapter a day, glossed, with questions.

groups.title: A2-B1: modern Hebrew, made easy
groups.note: Today's Hebrew, simplified for new immigrants and for Israeli kids. The easiest real Hebrew there is.

items.title: סִיפּוּרֵי דּוּאוֹלִינְגוֹ
items.author: duostories.org
items.blurb: 24 short dialogue stories built for English speakers, with audio and a question between the lines. Free, no account.

items.title: חַדְשׁוֹן בְּעִבְרִית קַלָּה
items.en: Hadshon: the news in easy Hebrew
items.author: Ministry of Education
items.blurb: The weekly news for new immigrants, the paper that replaced Sha'ar LaMatchil. Hard words carry their points and a Hebrew explanation. A new issue every week.

items.title: חַדְשׁוֹן לִילָדִים
items.author: Ministry of Education
items.blurb: The news page Israeli schools give 9-12 year olds: partly pointed, words explained, some articles read aloud.

items.title: שַׁעַר לַמַּתְחִיל
items.author: Ministry of Education
items.blurb: The pointed easy-Hebrew paper olim read from 1956 to 2012. Ten years of issues, free. The news is old; the Hebrew is not.

items.title: וִיקִיקִידְס
items.author: Israeli kids
items.blurb: The encyclopedia Israeli children write for each other. Pick any topic and read the opening.
items.note: No points: the place to practise reading without them.

groups.title: B1: Israeli children's classics
groups.note: Written in Hebrew for Israeli children, from the first Tel Aviv on. Modern Hebrew, and stories every Israeli grew up with.

items.title: הַשּׁוּעָל הַמְעוֹפֵף
items.author: Levin Kipnis
items.blurb: An animal story for small children by Levin Kipnis, who wrote many of the holiday songs Israeli kindergartens still sing. Fully pointed.

items.title: הַחוֹפֶשׁ הַגָּדוֹל, אוֹ: תַּעֲלוּמַת הָאַרְגָּזִים
items.en: The long holiday, or the mystery of the crates
items.author: Nahum Gutman
items.blurb: Two schoolboys, Nahum and Ran, spend the summer in Rehovot during the First World War, under the Turks, and stumble on a mystery. A short novel for children.

items.title: שְׁבִיל קְלִיפּוֹת הַתַּפּוּזִים
items.author: Nahum Gutman
items.blurb: Tel Aviv in the First World War, its people driven out. Nahum, fifteen, slips back in on a secret errand: money the town hid under a floor before it left. Gutman's own boyhood, told for children.

items.title: אַנְשֵׁי בְּרֵאשִׁית
items.author: Eliezer Shmali
items.blurb: The Zeid family, pioneer watchmen, settle alone on a hill in the Jezreel valley. Written for children in 1933 and a classic ever since.

groups.title: B1: legends and fables
groups.note: The legends every Israeli child knows, retold for children. Bialik wrote his in a Biblical style: the table above covers it.

items.title: אֲתַר הָאַגָּדָה לִילָדִים
items.author: Snunit, Hebrew University
items.blurb: Over a hundred legends of the Sages retold for children, illustrated, and every one read aloud. Listen once, then read.

items.title: מִשְׁלֵי אִיסוֹפּוֹס
items.author: Aesop, trans. Shlomo Spann
items.blurb: The fox and the grapes and a hundred more, a paragraph each: the shortest complete stories in this list.

items.title: שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ וְהַדְּבוֹרָה
items.author: H. N. Bialik
items.blurb: A bee stings the sleeping king and he lets her go. Years later the Queen of Sheba sets him a test no wisdom can pass, and the bee pays him back.

items.title: אַגָּדַת שְׁלוֹשָׁה וְאַרְבָּעָה
items.en: The legend of three and four
items.author: H. N. Bialik
items.blurb: Solomon reads in the stars that his daughter will marry a pauper and locks her in a tower on an island. Fate finds a way. The longest and best loved of Bialik's legends.

items.title: אַלּוּף בְּצָלוֹת וְאַלּוּף שׁוּם
items.en: The prince of onions and the prince of garlic
items.author: H. N. Bialik
items.blurb: A merchant brings a faraway king something his land has never tasted and sails home rich; an envious rival tries to do better. Rhymed prose in twelve short chapters, a children's classic.

groups.title: B1+: classics in Hebrew translation
groups.note: Translated, not written in Hebrew: stories you already know, which makes them the easiest long reads here. Old translations, so old spelling.

items.title: בַּת הַמֶּלֶךְ עַל הָעֲדָשָׁה
items.author: H. C. Andersen, trans. David Frishman
items.blurb: The princess who cannot sleep on a single lentil, here, rather than a pea. One page: the shortest Andersen.

items.title: בִּגְדֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ הַחֲדָשִׁים
items.author: H. C. Andersen, trans. David Frishman
items.blurb: Two swindlers, a cloth nobody can see, and the child who says so out loud.

items.title: הַזָּמִיר
items.author: H. C. Andersen, trans. David Frishman
items.blurb: The emperor of China prefers a clockwork bird to the real one, until he is dying.

items.title: שׁוּלְחָן עָרוּךְ, חֲמוֹר זָהָב וּמַקֵּל
items.en: The wishing table, the gold donkey and the cudgel
items.author: Brothers Grimm, trans. David Frishman
items.blurb: Three brothers, three magic gifts, and an innkeeper who steals two of them. Frishman gave everyone Hebrew names.

items.title: מָעוֹת שֶׁל חֲנוּכָּה
items.author: Sholem Aleichem, trans. Y. D. Berkowitz
items.blurb: Two small brothers make the rounds of the relatives collecting Hanukkah coins, and count them after every visit. Translated from Yiddish by the author's son-in-law.

items.title: עֲלִי בָּאבָּא וְאַרְבָּעִים הַשּׁוֹדְדִים
items.en: Ali Baba and the forty thieves
items.author: The Thousand and One Nights, trans. Y. Y. Rivlin
items.blurb: Open sesame. From Rivlin's Thousand and One Nights, fully pointed.

items.title: הַנָּסִיךְ הַקָּטָן
items.author: Saint-Exupéry, trans. Arie Lerner
items.blurb: The pilot, the boy from a very small planet, the fox and the rose. Plain Hebrew, short chapters, and you know the story.

items.title: פִּינוֹקְיוֹ
items.author: Carlo Collodi, trans. Yisrael Dushman
items.blurb: The wooden boy whose nose gives him away. A whole book in short chapters.

items.title: מוֹטְל בֶּן פֵּייסִי הַחַזָּן
items.author: Sholem Aleichem, trans. Y. D. Berkowitz
items.blurb: An orphan boy tells, cheerfully, how his family loses everything and sets off for America. A book, but every chapter stands alone.

groups.title: B2: Israeli short stories
groups.note: Grown-up fiction in the Hebrew Israelis actually speak, from the 1900s to the 1950s. Mostly unpointed: switch the points off in the app first and get used to it.

items.title: הַיְרוּשָּׁה, פְּרָקִים ו-י
items.author: HaMachberet
items.blurb: The second half of the serial: a lawyer's drawer, a biscuit tin of letters, and what the grandmother had arranged. The bridge into B2.

items.title: חוֹלוֹת הַזָּהָב
items.author: Binyamin Tammuz
items.blurb: A boy walks alone in the sand dunes, remembering his mother. The title story of Tammuz's first book, and there is a recording to read along with.

items.title: אוֹפֶק
items.author: Binyamin Tammuz
items.blurb: The smallest of forty children on his way to school, and the class that never lets him forget it.

items.title: תַּחֲרוּת שְׂחִיָּיה
items.author: Binyamin Tammuz
items.blurb: A Jewish boy spends a day in the orange grove of a grateful Arab family and loses a swimming race to their son, Abdul-Karim. He comes back to the same grove in 1948. One of the best known Israeli short stories.

items.title: חַדְרָה
items.author: Moshe Smilansky
items.blurb: Stories of the first Jewish villages and their Arab neighbours, by a farmer who lived in Rehovot from 1890. Start with this one; the author page has dozens more.

groups.title: B2: the classics, 1890-1930
groups.note: The generation that made Hebrew a literature again, before it was a spoken language. Older words and old spelling: read them for the stories.

items.title: אִם לֹא לְמַעְלָה מִזֶּה
items.author: Y. L. Peretz
items.blurb: Every year before the High Holidays the rebbe of Nemirov disappears, and the town says he goes up to heaven. A sceptic from Lithuania hides under his bed to see where he really goes. Every Israeli reads it at school.

items.title: שָׁלוֹשׁ מַתָּנוֹת
items.author: Y. L. Peretz
items.blurb: A soul is turned away at the gate of heaven and sent back to find three gifts worth bringing. A folk tale, dark and moving.

items.title: בּוֹנְצִי שְׁתוֹק
items.author: Y. L. Peretz, trans. Shimshon Meltzer
items.blurb: A man who never once complained arrives in heaven, and is told he may have anything he wants.

items.title: יָגוֹן
items.author: Anton Chekhov, trans. Devorah Baron
items.blurb: A sledge driver whose son has died spends a snowy night looking for someone who will listen. Translated by one of the best Hebrew stylists of her day.

items.title: כְּרִיתוּת
items.author: Devorah Baron
items.blurb: Ten years married and no child: by the law of the town the couple must part. Baron's women of the shtetl, told without a wasted word.

items.title: הַחֲצוֹצְרָה נִתְבַּיְּישָׁה
items.author: H. N. Bialik
items.blurb: A Jewish family in a Russian village, a decree against them, and a trumpet. Bialik's last story, and his plainest.

items.title: מֵאֲחוֹרֵי הַגָּדֵר
items.author: H. N. Bialik
items.blurb: Noah, a Jewish boy, and Marinka, the orphan girl in the yard next door, and the fence their families keep between them. Bialik's best known story.

items.title: סָפִיחַ
items.author: H. N. Bialik
items.blurb: Bialik remembers being very small: the village, the forest, the first fears. Lyrical and slow, the hardest Bialik here.

items.title: תְּמוּנוֹת מִבֵּית מְבַשֵּׁל הַשֵּׁכָר
items.author: Asher Barash
items.blurb: A Jewish woman runs the brewery of a small Galician town, and the town's whole life passes through her yard. A short novel in scenes.

groups.title: B2+: three Bible stories, side by side
groups.note: Archaic Hebrew: the vav that flips the tense, old words, old spelling. Read them for the stories Israelis quote, not as a model for your own Hebrew.

items.title: יוֹנָה
items.author: The book of Jonah
items.blurb: A prophet runs from God, spends three days inside a fish, and sulks when the city he warned is spared. Four short chapters: the easiest whole book.

items.title: רוּת
items.author: The book of Ruth
items.blurb: A widow follows her mother-in-law to Bethlehem: your people shall be my people. Mostly dialogue, and gentle.

items.title: דָּוִד וְגוֹלְיָית
items.author: 1 Samuel 17
items.blurb: A shepherd boy, five stones and a giant. Armour, insults and long speeches.
